title: Machine learning reveals common features of unconventional superconductors with high transition temperatures
authors: Haosheng Xu, Dongheng Qian, Yijun Yu, Jing Wang
abstract: Superconductors with high critical temperatures that emerges beyond the phonon-mediated regime are usually considered unconventional in nature, yet unlike conventional superconductors, no broadly applicable predictive theory currently guides their discovery. Here, we use interpretable machine learning to uncover a common materials-space signature of high-$T_{\mathrm{c}}$ unconventional superconductors and develop a data-driven strategy for materials discovery. We construct a unified feature representation for each material by integrating compositional statistics, structural information, and latent representations from trained property-prediction models, followed by structure-aware filtering of an experimentally established superconducting dataset. Without using transition-temperature information, unsupervised analysis shows that cuprate and iron-based superconductors occupy a common region of materials space, characterized primarily by large electronegativity deviation and intermediate mean valence-electron number. A supervised $T_{\text{c}}$ model independently identifies the same descriptors as dominant features, providing complementary evidence for their relevance. Using this empirical materials-space prior together with the $T_{\text{c}}$ model, we prioritize candidate materials, recover recently discovered nickelate superconductors, and identify chemically distinct candidates for future investigation.
summary: This work uses machine learning to bypass the need for a fundamental theory of high-Tc superconductivity. By analyzing structural and chemical features of known materials, the authors identified key empirical signatures—specifically large electronegativity deviation and intermediate valence electron counts—that characterize these complex superconductors. This data-driven prior allows for the prediction and prioritization of entirely new candidate materials.
main_problem: To find a common, data-driven materials-space signature for high-Tc unconventional superconductors, as no broadly applicable predictive theory currently guides their discovery.
main_result: The analysis revealed that high-Tc unconventional superconductors cluster in a materials space characterized by large electronegativity deviation and intermediate mean valence-electron numbers.
method: The study employed interpretable machine learning, integrating compositional, structural, and latent electronic representations to perform unsupervised clustering and supervised $T_c$ prediction.
model_or_system: The focus is on unconventional superconductors, particularly cuprate and iron-based families, analyzed using a unified feature vector combining 120+ dimensions from elemental properties, crystal structure, and ALIGNN-derived embeddings.
key_observables: Critical temperature ($T_c$), average deviation of electronegativity, and mean number of valence electrons.
important_parameters: Intermediate mean valence-electron number ($\approx 7-8$); large electronegativity deviation.
main_assumptions: The approach avoids assuming a particular microscopic pairing mechanism, relying instead on empirical correlations within the materials space.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ML workflow, the clustering of superconducting materials in the feature space (PC1-PC2 plane), and the correlation of $T_c$ with the key descriptors.
paper_structure: The paper follows a workflow: 1) Constructing a high-dimensional feature vector; 2) Curating the dataset; 3) Performing unsupervised analysis (PCA) to find common regions; and 4) Using supervised learning to confirm feature importance and prioritize new candidates.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state materials, the use of ML to extract robust, generalizable descriptors from complex electronic and structural data mirrors approaches used in modeling strongly correlated quantum systems where first-principles calculations are intractable.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: Figure 1. Overview of the machine-learning workflow. a, Construction of a unified 147-dimensional feature vector from composition-derived descriptors, structure-derived descriptors, and latent representations extracted from pre-trained ALIGNN models. b, Dataset curation through structure-aware filtering, and organization of the descriptors into feature groups by hierarchical clustering. c, Unsupervised PCA analysis, supervised Tc prediction with feature importance analysis, and candidate screening.

Figure 2. Unsupervised analysis of the superconducting materials space. a, Projection of the curated superconducting dataset onto the PC1–PC2 plane. Cu-based and iron-based families concentrate in a common region (ellipse), into which La3Ni2O7 (triangle), Nd0.8Sr0.2NiO2 (circle) and RbSr2PdO3 (star), all of which are outside the training set, also fall. b,c, Relationships between PC1 and avg dev Electronegativity (b) and between PC2 and mean NValence (c), with colors as in a.
Figure 3. Dependence of Tc on the two leading descriptors. a, Tc versus avg dev Electronegativity. The inset shows the iron-based subfamilies separately. b, Tc versus mean NValence.

Figure 4. Supervised prediction of Tc. a, Predicted versus experimental Tc under five-fold cross-validation (MAE = 3.28 K, R2 = 0.931); the dashed line marks perfect prediction. b,c, Experimental and out-of-fold predicted Tc values for (b) cuprate and (c) iron-based superconductors obtained from five-fold cross-validation. d, The eight most important feature groups for Tc prediction.

Figure 5. Two-step screening of potential superconducting candidates. Materials from the Materials Project database are first filtered by their position in the PC1–PC2 plane, and the retained candidates are then ranked by predicted Tc, post- screened into two targeted subsets (sets A and B), and examined through literature mining assisted by large language models.
